title: RAG from Scratch
blurb: Build retrieval-augmented generation one primitive at a time: chunking, embeddings, retrieval, context packing, citation checks and retrieval evaluation, then wire them into one pipeline.
intro: Retrieval-augmented generation answers a question from documents the model was never trained on. Each step builds one stage and tests it on its own: split documents into overlapping chunks, turn chunks into TF-IDF vectors, rank them with hybrid retrieval, pack the best evidence into a token budget with permission checks, verify that every cited chunk supports its sentence, and measure whether retrieval found the expected evidence. The capstone composes the stages into a deterministic extractive pipeline. In a framework such as LangChain these map onto a text splitter, an embedding model with a vector store such as Chroma, a retriever, a prompt template and an LLM call.
